Name: Steve
March2025_walk_notes:
No flooding issues lately w/ new sewers. FEMA came out 30 years ago after severe flooding to provide new pumps and some elevation. New gutter system good as long as its kept clean, he's a plumber so he has replaced pump himself 2x over 30 years. Automatic sump pumps that drain to thr street. Goes off every time it rains 1/2 inch or more. 1st rain or two of the season not an issue, but by the 3rd and beyond, the sump pump will go off every time it rains even a drop because the ground is so soaked. Back in the day, had water up to lawn and garage and halfway into the street. This year was unusual in that there was a pool of water in the backyard - 8ft diameter circle like a little pond. Not too deep but easily covers shoes and up to ankle. First time in 20+ years.

Did some new landscaping this year, added concrete patio - maybe that's causing rthe pooling? Nowhere for water to drain. FEMA 30 yrs ago provided clips/beams for under the foundation. 10 or so years ago, City added check valves to prevent sewage backflows. Not a concern at his house right now.
